title: D6 Video Games for fans of Dungeon Dive Board Games
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w6b2AkddE8Y

Daniel (@dungeondive) steps off the usual path with six video games he reaches for when he wants a board game but not the setup — mostly modern roguelites heavy on random events, ranked roughly by how much they feel like something on the table.

- **Children of Morta** (Dead Mage) — action-heavy family roguelite with gorgeous modern pixel art and real emotional weight.
- **Curious Expedition 2** (Maschinen-Mensch) — pulp explorers' club hex crawl with dice-driven encounters; *Robinson Crusoe* fans take note.
- **Citizen Sleeper** (Jump Over the Age) — a cyberpunk dice-placement narrative game; compelling world, rough prose and clunky interface.
- **Guild of Dungeoneering** (Gambrinous) — the graph-paper meta-RPG that *D6: Dungeons, Dames, Dice & Danger* promised and missed; you build the dungeon from cards to lure your adventurer.
- **Tangledeep** (Impact Gameworks) — a traditional turn-based roguelike with deep systems, monster pets and item dungeons; a *Gloomhaven*/*Mage Knight* level of commitment.
- **For the King** (IronOak) — his number one. If it were a board game it would be his favourite of all time, and six unmanageable boxes; think *Runebound* with every expansion, twice.

His one gripe with *For the King* is the slow meta-progression — the carrot is on a slightly too-long stick.

----

Which video game scratches your board game itch best — and is there one you'd genuinely rather play on a screen than on the table?
